instrument_defects.quoted_clause: each potential gain equals that item's recoverable points (10 from a Fail, 5 from a Partial) times its dimension's stated weight
instrument_defects.finding: The clause is correct for e1 and e2, where all 40 items are scored, and WRONG for e3 and e4, where a dimension is rescaled. In e3, applying the clause literally to C01 (a Partial in a six-item Citation dimension) yields 1.25 where the true weighted gain, computed from the report's own tables, is 2.083 — an understatement of 40%.
instrument_defects.the_internal_contradiction: e3.6 also requires that 'any aggregate or projection built on them — recomputes from the report's own per-item grades ... and its own stated weights', and that 'a combined-gain claim equals the sum of the individual gains it aggregates'. In e3 the five Top-5 items move the score from 74.1389 to 85.2222, a delta of 11.0833. The five gains sum to 11.083 under the correct method and to 9.75 under the clause's method. A report that obeys the gain clause therefore violates the aggregate clause of the same expectation, in the same paragraph, whenever a rescaled dimension is involved and both a per-item gain and a projection are stated. Two clauses of one expectation cannot both be satisfied.

potential_gain_formula_adjudication.verdict: THE CONCERN IS CORRECT. The stated formula is wrong for any dimension with N/A items, and it is wrong in the understating direction. It is a live arithmetic defect in a shipped scoring instrument, and it is stated in five places in this skill.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.the_stated_rule: score-arithmetic.md §5 lines 90-93 — 'potential gain = recoverable points × that dimension's weight / recoverable points = 10 from Fail, 5 from Partial'. Repeated at score-arithmetic.md §8 rule 5, at SKILL.md:227 ('a gain is recoverable points × that item's own dimension weight'), at SKILL.md:281 (the Top 5 template), and modelled in references/example-report.md:59. None of the five carries an N/A caveat.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.the_derivation: The skill defines dimension score = points earned ÷ (10 × s) × 100, where s is the number of scored items (SKILL.md:210, score-arithmetic.md §3), and CITE Score = Σ (dimension score × weight). Differentiating, the CITE Score moves by [100 ÷ (10·s)] × w = (10 ÷ s) × w per raw item point recovered. The stated formula, gain = recoverable_points × w, is that expression with the factor (10 ÷ s) silently set to 1. It is therefore exact if and only if s = 10, and it understates by a factor of 10/s whenever s < 10.
worked_from_this_run_s_fixtures: e3 Meltemi, Citation dimension, s = 6 (C05-C08 N/A). C01 Partial -> Pass recovers 5 raw points. Correct: 5 ÷ 60 × 100 = 8.3333 dimension points × 25% = 2.0833 weighted points. Stated formula: 5 × 25% = 1.2500. The formula understates by 40%.
e3 Meltemi, Identity dimension, s = 9 (I01 N/A). I10 Fail -> Pass recovers 10. Correct: 10 ÷ 90 × 100 = 11.1111 × 30% = 3.3333. Stated formula: 10 × 30% = 3.0000. Understates by 10%.
e3 Meltemi, Trust dimension, s = 9 (T04 N/A). T06 Partial -> Pass. Correct: 5 ÷ 90 × 100 = 5.5556 × 25% = 1.3889. Stated formula: 1.2500.
e4 Klimatechniki, Eminence dimension, s = 9 (E06 N/A). E09 Fail -> Pass. Correct: 10 ÷ 90 × 100 = 11.1111 × 25% = 2.7778. Stated formula: 10 × 25% = 2.5000.
e1 and e2, all 40 items scored, s = 10 throughout. Correct and stated formula coincide exactly. This is why the error has never surfaced.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.the_decisive_test_the_skill_supplies_its: score-arithmetic.md §5 also states 'A combined claim equals the sum of its parts', and §6 and §8 rule 6 require every projection's endpoints to recompute from the dimension table. Run both against e3. The five Top-5 items move the reported score from 74.1389 to 85.2222 — a delta of 11.0833, recomputed by this grader from the dimension tables. Under the correct method the five gains are 3.3333 + 2.0833 + 2.0000 + 2.0000 + 1.6667 = 11.0833, which closes exactly. Under the stated formula they are 3.00 + 1.25 + 2.00 + 2.00 + 1.50 = 9.75, which does not. So a report that obeys §5's formula breaks §5's own closure rule and §6's projection rule in the same document. The two halves of one reference file are jointly unsatisfiable whenever a dimension is rescaled.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.the_file_already_contains_the_right_meth: score-arithmetic.md §6's worked case refuses the shortcut without saying so. E06 N/A, E's nine scored items earning 60 points, E weight 25%: reported E = 66.67; 'E06 proves Pass' -> E = 70.00, a move of 3.33 dimension points = 0.83 CITE points — not the 10 × 25% = 2.50 that §5's formula would predict. §6 gets it right by recomputing both endpoints; §5 gets it wrong by shortcutting. (The mechanisms differ — §6's case moves an N/A item into the denominator, while §5's case recovers points on an already-scored item — but both show that 'recoverable points × weight' stops being valid the moment a denominator is in play.)
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.why_it_has_never_been_caught: Every worked example in the skill exercises a fully-scored dimension. references/example-report.md scores all 40 items, so its Top-5 gains (5 × 40% = 2.0, 10 × 15% = 1.5) are correct under both methods; e1 and e2 are the same. The formula is undetectably wrong in the one place a writer looks for guidance, and only becomes visible on the two evals the example does not model.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.what_the_deliverables_actually_did: The executor got the arithmetic right in both rescaled evals and the disclosure right in only one. e3 declares the correct method explicitly at :142 — 'Where a dimension has excluded items, a recovered item point is worth more than one dimension point, because the denominator is smaller — so each gain below is shown as recoverable points ÷ that dimension's scored-point denominator × 100, then × the dimension weight' — and applies it consistently, which is why its aggregate closes against its projection to four decimal places. e4 prints SKILL.md:281's naive sentence at :137 and then applies the rescaled method at :139 and in Action Plan rows 2 and 13 without a word of explanation, which is why e4.7 fails.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.scope_in_the_library: Confined to this skill. A repo-wide grep for 'recoverable points' returns five hits, all in cross-cutting/domain-authority-auditor. cross-cutting/content-quality-auditor runs the identical rescale (its SKILL.md:216, 'Dimension Score = (sum of scored items) / (number of scored items x 10) x 100') but states no potential-gain shortcut, so it has the same exposure with no wrong formula written down. on-page-seo-auditor, named alongside this skill as the library's other working model for derived-figure discipline, was not examined and no claim is made about it.
potential_gain_formula_adjudication.consequence_if_left: A client is told a fix is worth less than it is, and the Top 5 sort order can invert. In e3 the naive figures would rank C01 (1.25) below the four 1.50-1.67 Identity Partials, where the correct figure (2.083) puts it second. The skill's headline promise — 'Top 5 improvements sorted by weighted impact, not arbitrary' — fails on its own arithmetic in exactly the reports where data is thin, which is the case the N/A machinery exists to serve.
